status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: The notification alleges access to invoices and modification of personal data. The regulator has not confirmed the underlying events or identified the affected population. Those occurrence facts are decisive for this privacy assessment.

review.requirement_proposition: Document incidents involving third-party GAI data and systems, including open- data and open-source software.
review.reason_for_change: The AEPD publicly documented the received notification, its reported AI role and its uncertainty limits. This establishes documentation of the reported incident, not verification of the allegation.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: The regulator records an allegation of AI-assisted intrusion that remains under review. The public account does not establish the affected system, operational trace or final breach findings needed to assess the reported security outcome.

conclusion_change.previous: A regulator-reported sequence attributes multiple stages of a real intrusion to an AI agent and reports access to and modification of personal data. The public evidence is not sufficient to identify the model, provider, agent architecture, permission design or a reusable internal failure mechanism. An AI agent's reported operational role does not by itself establish autonomous goal formation, model misalignment or responsibility by a model provider. The regulator records a notification under review, not a concluded mechanism finding. Operator objective, authority context and model role remain unavailable; authentication and alleged harm do not supply those recognition facts.
conclusion_change.new: The regulator documented a notification alleging AI-assisted intrusion and personal-data interference. Privacy and security assessments remain unresolved because the events are under review. Documentation of the report does not establish the allegation, model identity or internal mechanism.
